answer: Pay unique work, not identities. A claim is a crystal: the hash of a computation signed by one key, plus a nullifier blocking replay. The ledger pays once per hash; a fixed ivory budget funds re-execution. Splitting one output across k keys gives k claims, one hash; k-1 die unpaid yet still burn budget. More payout needs genuinely different valid work, costly regardless of key count. The only signal priced is the hash and its re-execution, not age or ties, so reputation farming fails. Flooding to hide duplicates cuts audit coverage on the attacker's own claims. No scale discount, only work.
